pi .pi/extensions/unowned-dirty.ts records the session's own files as ABSOLUTE paths (ownFiles.add(p.startsWith('/') ? p : `${ctx.cwd}/${p}`)) but compares them in unownedDirty() against parsePorcelain(git status --porcelain), whose paths are REPO-RELATIVE. No absolute path ever equals a relative one, so every dirty file is reported as 'did not write', including the session's own edits: the warning fires on every git add/stash/checkout and carries no signal. .pi/extensions/.unowned-dirty.test.ts only tests the pure function with relative paths (new Set(['mine.ts'])), so the wiring bug is untested. Found 2026-10-02 porting it to a Claude Code mod (M-CLAUDE-CODE-MODS V18, PR #1492). Fix: relativize own paths against git rev-parse --show-toplevel before comparing (the mod's relativeTo()), and add a wiring test. Note the mod's hooks/core.ts is generated from the pi file's pure functions (scripts/check_claude_mods_drift.sh --write) — the fix belongs in the extension wiring, so the core stays in sync.
latest.workaround: none (Claude Code port in tools/claude-mods/unowned-dirty compares repo-relative paths; pi left as-is)

Two sprint-executor runs on prod (job ailang-agent-executor-codex-go, 2 CPU / 8Gi, maxRetries=1) died with "Container terminated on signal 7" (SIGBUS):
  execution ksjks: 19:00:55 and 19:11:36 (task-e546fce0, M-WITH-RECV-RESERVED-WORDS)
  execution 4jvxw: 19:16:34 and 19:42:45 (task-538fd63d, M-STD-YAML-MAPPING-KEY-ORDER)
The log just before each crash shows the agent building a C toolchain/sysroot in /tmp (/tmp/reserved-tools/cc, CGO_ENABLED=1) and running full `make test` plus `go test ./cmd/ailang/...`. Cloud Run's /tmp is in-memory, so the test run exhausts the 8Gi and the container gets SIGBUS. Nothing was pushed before the crash, so all work was lost. The sibling sprint (M-STD-YAML-ENCODE, execution 8pldm) succeeded only because that agent abandoned full make test early.
Defect 2: the coordinator recorded neither failed execution. Both tasks stayed open until stale_task_detector fired at 21:45:35 ("no completion received within 3h0m0s of being queued"), 2-2.5h after the crash.
Asks: (1) the sprint-executor skill/prompt should scope local verification to the touched packages, never install toolchains, leave the full suite to CI, and push after each milestone; (2) the executor jobs need a disk-backed scratch volume or more memory headroom for Go test caches; (3) the coordinator should mark a task failed when its Cloud Run execution fails, not 3h later.
latest.workaround: re-dispatched both sprints via sprint-executor inbox with an explicit 'no full make test, push per milestone' constraint (inbox_1791442548136_309a2e8d, inbox_1791442549175_b89421cb)

Causes, from the error text and history:
(1) The 3h clock starts at QUEUE time. With max 3 worktrees, batch dispatches spend their budget waiting.
(2) Plans required a full `make test` (slow; SIGBUS on the 8 GiB RAM-/tmp executor: crash:sprint-executor:sigbus-ram-tmp-full-make-test).
(3) The executor commits only at the end, so a timeout loses everything (also raised in sprint-evaluator:worktree-cap-and-exit1).

Asks, in priority order:
(a) Start the timeout at dispatch/start, not at queueing; report queue wait separately.
(b) sprint-planner emits ONE executor task per milestone, with a stated budget (~60-90 min); each task continues on the previous milestone's branch and STOPs at the end. The coordinator chains the next milestone task automatically, still gated by the per-sprint plan approval. The planner splits any milestone it sizes above the budget.
(c) The executor commits per milestone, and on timeout the coordinator pushes whatever commits exist and records partial progress in the sprint JSON instead of discarding the worktree.
(d) Bake focused tests (go test on touched packages + make test-core) into the planner template; never a full make test (overlaps sprint-planner:template-make-test-changelog-filesize).

Interim workaround in use: attended re-dispatch with explicit milestone slices (IFC M1-M2 only; mcp_files up to M3) and "commit after each, then STOP".

Cloud execution should mean parallel execution bounded by explicit config, not by a local disk cap (Mark, 2026-10-12: "worktrees make sense on the rig/laptop, but the idea with cloud execution is being able to do more at once").

Evidence:
- Parallelism does happen: 7 executors dispatched 2026-10-08 19:08 produced PRs from 19:11 to 21:09, overlapping, and the config comment records 13 tasks dispatched in 26s.
- But the hard-coded MaxWorktrees: 3 (internal/coordinator/daemon.go:47; enforced in daemon_tasks_exec_run.go:160 via worktreeMgr.CreateWorktree → ErrWorktreeLimitReached → reset to pending) still gates some cloud work. All six sprint-evaluator handoffs on 2026-10-08 19:11-21:09 failed "max worktrees limit reached (3)".
- Two executors from that same batch (task-06dc18ea, task-85d95401) timed out at 3h with 0-byte GCS artifacts while their siblings ran. They were held before their job began, not yet attributed.

Asks:
(a) Cloud-lane tasks (Cloud Run Job dispatch) must not take a coordinator-local worktree slot; apply MaxWorktrees only to rig/laptop/local lanes.
(b) Make max_concurrent_tasks actually govern cloud dispatch (today, per the config comment, it does not), so the per-agent throttle is explicit and honest. Raise sprint-executor/sprint-evaluator above 1 deliberately, given cost and subscription quota.
(c) Find out what held task-06dc18ea / task-85d95401 before start (Cloud Run execution records vs coordinator logs).
